summary.text: Greg Stanton is the Democratic incumbent for Arizona's 4th Congressional District. An attorney by training, he served on the Phoenix City Council, as Arizona deputy attorney general and as mayor of Phoenix from 2012 to 2018 before his election to the U.S. House in 2018. He serves on the Transportation and Infrastructure and Foreign Affairs committees and is seeking another term.

paragraphs.text: Stanton was born on Long Island, New York, in 1970 and graduated from Cortez High School in Arizona.

He earned a B.A. in political science and history from Marquette University in 1992, which his official biography says he attended on a Harry S. Truman Scholarship, and a J.D. from the University of Michigan in 1995. He worked as an attorney before and between public offices.
Stanton served on the Phoenix City Council from 2000 to 2009, which his official biography describes as nine years, and then as Arizona's deputy attorney general from 2009 to 2010.

He was mayor of Phoenix from 2012 to 2018. His official biography says he focused on innovation and trade, bioscience and higher education investments, and a voter-approved public transportation plan that funded light rail expansion, faster bus service and road modernization.

Stanton was elected to the U.S. House in 2018 and represented Arizona's 9th District until redistricting placed him in the 4th District for the 2022 election. He served on the Judiciary Committee from 2019 to 2022.

For 2025-2026 his committee assignments are Transportation and Infrastructure, with subcommittees on Aviation; Economic Development, Public Buildings and Emergency Management; and Highways and Transit, along with Foreign Affairs and the Select Committee on the Strategic Competition Between the United States and the Chinese Communist Party.

His official biography says he co-founded a congressional caucus on heat-related policy, was named Most Effective Democrat on Transportation Policy by the Center for Effective Lawmaking in 2025, and was named 2025 Elected Leader of the Year by the AZ AFL-CIO. It also says he is a husband and father of two children living in Arizona.
